info.title: squirrelscan Public API
info.summary: Programmatic website-audit API for external clients, agents, and MCP integrations.
info.description:
The public `/v1` REST surface of squirrelscan.

This document covers the **external-client-facing** routes only — internal
server-to-server callbacks (`/v1/*/internal/*`), webhook receivers
(`/v1/webhooks`, `/v1/github`), and admin-only routes (`/v1/admin/*`,
`/v1/stats`, `/v1/users`) are intentionally out of scope and NOT part of the
public contract.

All error responses use a stable typed envelope:
`{ "error": { "code": string, "message": string, "requestId"?: string } }`.

Authentication is via a bearer token in the `Authorization` header.
Organization API keys with an `sq_` prefix (`sq_dev_` in development) are the
primary mechanism for automated clients and agents; set one as the
`SQUIRRELSCAN_API_KEY` environment variable and the CLI and this REST API both
pick it up. CLI login tokens (`sqcli_`) and Clerk dashboard JWTs are also
accepted. MCP clients can reach these same audit tools over the hosted MCP
server at https://mcp.squirrelscan.com/mcp.

tags.name: Audits
tags.description: Create and track cloud audit runs (`agent_runs`).

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Publish, list, and manage audit reports.

tags.name: Credits
tags.description: Read the active organization's credit balance and pricing.

post.description: Start a new cloud audit run. With `trigger: "api"` the run is dispatched to the cloud crawler immediately and progresses asynchronously; poll `GET /v1/agent-runs/{id}` for status. Cloud features are credit-gated. If the requested page count exceeds the org's plan ceiling, the run still starts at the plan's max (clamp, never a hard error) and the response carries a `notice` field (`type: "page_limit_clamped"`) saying so.

502.description: Failed to dispatch the cloud audit (upstream crawler/sandbox unavailable). Typed envelope with code `UPSTREAM_ERROR`; the upstream cause is carried under `error.reason`.

get.description: List the authenticated user's audit runs, newest first.

Fetch full detail for a single audit run owned by the authenticated user. While `status` is `pending`/`running`, `progress` carries the latest phase/page-count event streamed by the run, when one has been recorded. `notice` carries a `page_limit_clamped` signal when the run's requested page count was clamped down to the org's plan ceiling at dispatch time (never a hard error — the run itself still completed normally).

Fetch the summarized report data for a completed run.

**Polling pattern:** this endpoint returns `404` both when the run/report does not exist AND while a valid run's report is not generated yet. To distinguish the two, poll `GET /v1/agent-runs/{id}` and wait for `status: "completed"` before fetching the report — that is the canonical way to track progress. As a convenience, the "not ready yet" 404 additionally carries the run's current status under `error.runStatus` (e.g. `{ "error": { "code": "NOT_FOUND", "message": "Report not available yet", "runStatus": "running" } }`), so a client can keep polling this endpoint alone if it prefers. **Footgun:** only keep polling while `error.runStatus` is a non-terminal state (`pending`/`running`); a `404` with `error.runStatus: "completed"` (or `"failed"`/`"cancelled"`, or a `404` with NO `error.runStatus` at all) means the report is genuinely missing/unavailable — stop polling.

200.description: Report summary + scored issues for the run.

404.description: Run or report not found, OR the run's report is not generated yet. When not-ready, `error.runStatus` holds the run's current status (`pending`/`running`/...); keep polling.

notFound.summary: Run or report does not exist

post.description: Publish an audit report. The report payload is the full `AuditReport` produced by the CLI/engine. Visibility defaults to `private`. **Publishing is included in the audit's base charge**; no visibility carries a separate credit charge. `unlisted` and `private` publishes always create a new report (no idempotency). Org-scoped `public` publishes are keyed on the publisher + a content hash: republishing the identical payload is an idempotent replay, returning the original report with `200` if the prior response was cached, or `409` otherwise (still in flight / not cached).

200.description: Idempotent replay of an identical org-scoped `public` publish whose original response was cached — returns the originally published report.

400.description: The body failed validation (`VALIDATION_ERROR`, with `error.issues`), was not valid JSON (`INVALID_JSON`), or tripped the content security scanner (`SECURITY_VIOLATION`, with `error.threats`).

get.description: List the authenticated user's published reports, newest first.
Fetch report metadata. Public and unlisted reports are readable without auth; private reports require a bearer token belonging to the owner (a non-owner gets 404, never revealing existence).

patch.description: Change a report's visibility. Owner only: a non-owner (or unauthenticated request) gets 404, never revealing the report's existence. Visibility changes carry no separate credit charge; publishing is included in the audit's base charge.

404.description: Report not found / not owned by the caller, OR — only when flipping to `public` — the report's stored content is missing from R2. Both use the typed envelope with code `NOT_FOUND`; branch on the 404 status.

notFound.summary: Report not found or not owned

get.description:
The graph of things the audited site declares in JSON-LD (Organization, Person, Product, Article, …), collapsed across every crawled page, with the references between them.

Filters apply BEFORE rendering, so `?type=Organization&format=markdown` renders a markdown document of Organizations rather than filtering a rendered string. `summary` always describes the WHOLE site even when a filter is applied; compare it against `meta.counts` to see whether you are holding a subset.

404 when the report predates the feature (no map was published with it), when it does not exist, or when it belongs to another organization. Available on every plan.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description:
Export format. `csv`, `dot`, `graphml` and `mermaid` are accepted but answer 501 until the `squirrel entities` command ships them.

Every value in the map is declared by the audited site, so treat it as untrusted. The `html` rendering escapes it and is safe to open directly. The `markdown` rendering escapes only table delimiters, which is sufficient while it is read as markdown: if you render it to HTML, sanitize it first, or use `format=json` and render the fields yourself.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Keep only entities carrying this schema.org `@type` (case-insensitive). Matched against EVERY type an entity declares, so an entity typed `["Organization", "LocalBusiness"]` matches either.

parameters.name: exclude_type
parameters.description:
Drop entities whose PRIMARY `@type` is exactly this one. Repeat the parameter to exclude several: `?exclude_type=WebPage&exclude_type=BreadcrumbList`.

Two differences from `type` above, both deliberate. It reads the primary type, `types[0]`, the one an entity leads with, rather than every type it declares: this expresses a deny-list over the one type an entity is listed under, which is what a viewer showing one chip per entity needs. And it is CASE-SENSITIVE, where `type` is not: the distinct primary types in a map are compared as strings, so a site declaring both `Organization` and `organization` has two of them, and folding case here would drop both when the caller named one.

The length bound is the published map's own `maxStringLength`, not the 128 that `type` uses, so every type name this endpoint can serve can also be excluded.

Combine freely with the other filters; they all apply before rendering.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description:
Keep only entities declared on this page URL, or on a page whose URL starts with it.

Matching is a plain prefix, so `https://site/about` also matches `https://site/about-us`; add a trailing slash to scope to a directory.

This filter can be INCOMPLETE. Each entity lists only its first few declaring pages (at most 5 in the published map this endpoint serves), with the rest collapsed into a `morePages` count, so an entity declared on 200 pages cannot match on one of the URLs that were not listed. When that is possible for the map being filtered, `meta.pageFilterIncomplete` is true.

parameters.name: problem
parameters.description: Keep only entities with this problem. `no-id`: no `@id`, so nothing ties the declarations together. `conflict`: occurrences disagree on a property. `dangling`: references an `@id` no page declares. `single-page`: declared on one page only. `split-identity`: the same thing declared under two different `@id`s.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text match over name, `@id`, key and types.

parameters.name: include_page_local
parameters.description: Include per-page types (BreadcrumbList, WebPage, ListItem, Question, Answer, and unnamed ImageObject). Off by default — they crowd out the entities the map exists to show.

200.description: The entity map. `application/json` for `format=json`; otherwise the requested rendering.

501.description: The requested export format is not implemented in this release.

get.summary: Get one entity from the report's entity map
get.description:
One node with its properties, occurrences, conflicts, declaring pages, and the edges pointing out of and into it.

`key` accepts the node key, the entity's `@id`, or its exact display name. An `@id` is a URL, so percent-encode it (`/` as `%2F`).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Node key, `@id`, or exact entity name. Percent-encode a URL.

get.description: Current credit balance for the active organization, plus the plan and the credit pricing table. Pass `?orgId=` to target a specific organization the caller is a member of.

parameters.name: orgId
parameters.description: Target a specific organization the caller belongs to. Defaults to the active org.

get.description: Read an organization the caller is a member of, including its members and plan limits.

Public and unauthenticated — streams the organization's logo image (PNG/JPEG/WebP) with its stored content type, or 404 when no logo is set. This is the stable URL that `organizations.avatarUrl` points to.

post.description: Owner/admin only. Multipart upload with a `file` field. Accepts PNG/JPEG/WebP validated by magic bytes (SVG and non-images are rejected regardless of declared content type), max 1MB. Stores the image and persists its public URL on `organizations.avatarUrl`.

file.description: PNG, JPEG, or WebP image, max 1MB.

200.description: Logo stored; returns the served URL.

415.description: The bytes are not a PNG/JPEG/WebP image (e.g. SVG). Typed envelope with code `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`.

error.message: Logo must be a PNG, JPEG, or WebP image

delete.description: Owner/admin only. Deletes the stored logo and clears `organizations.avatarUrl`.

bearerAuth.description:
Bearer token in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Programmatic API keys are prefixed `sq_` (issue #154; bearer auth lands in #156). The same scheme today also accepts CLI tokens (`sqcli_` prefix) and Clerk dashboard JWTs.

RateLimitLimit.description: Request quota for the current window.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests remaining in the current window.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until the current rate-limit window resets.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (sent on 429).

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid credentials (including the shared auth middleware: no/invalid bearer token). Typed envelope with code `UNAUTHORIZED`. Branch on the `401` status, not the message.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not permitted (e.g. not a member of the requested organization). Typed envelope; code `FORBIDDEN`, or `NO_ORG` when no active organization is resolved on credit/org-scoped routes. Branch on the `403` status.

forbidden.summary: Not permitted (e.g. API key scoped to a different org)

error.message: API key is not scoped to this organization

NotFound.description: Resource not found (or hidden from the caller).

ValidationError.description: Request body or query failed validation. `error.issues` lists up to 10 failed fields (`{ path, message }`); when more failed, `error.truncated: true` and `error.totalIssues` indicate the full count.

InsufficientCredits.description: The organization does not have enough credits for this operation. Typed envelope with code `INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS`; `error.required` and `error.balance` carry the credit detail. Branch on the `402` status.

balance.description: The org's credit balance at the time of the failure.

DuplicateRequest.description: An identical request was already processed under the same idempotency key and is still in flight or its cached response is unavailable. Typed envelope with code `DUPLICATE_REQUEST`.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body exceeds the maximum allowed size.

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. Retry after the window resets. (Rate limiting is planned — issue #69 — these headers document the intended contract.)

Error.description: Stable error envelope returned by all public routes.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE). Treat unknown codes as opaque.

message.description: Human-readable description. May change; do not match on it.

requestId.description: Correlation id for support / log lookups, when available.

trigger.description: Run origin. Public API callers must send `api`, which dispatches the cloud crawler. (`cli`/`github`/`scheduled` are internal-origin values that skip cloud dispatch and are not accepted here.)

config.description: Optional run config as a JSON-**encoded string** (not a nested object — the field is parsed server-side). Keys: coverageMode, maxPages, disabledRulePatterns, externalLinksEnabled. NOTE the round-trip asymmetry: you send a string here, but `AuditRun.config` is returned as a parsed object.

PageLimitClampNotice.description: Present only when the run's requested page count exceeded the org's plan ceiling. The run is never rejected for this (clamp-and-notify, not a hard error) — it dispatches at `applied` pages instead of `requested`, and this field says so.

requested.description: Pages that were actually asked for (stored crawl config or an explicit request override).

applied.description: Pages the run actually dispatched with — equal to `planCap`.

planCap.description: The org's plan's effective max-pages-per-audit ceiling at dispatch time.

upgradeHint.description: Human-readable upgrade suggestion, always including a pricing URL.

AuditRun.description: Full audit run record (the single-run GET). A caller can only fetch their own runs, so the owner identifiers below are always the caller's own. Composed as `AuditRunListItem` plus the owner identifiers `userId`/`orgId` via `allOf`, so the shared fields are defined once and cannot drift between the two.

userId.description: Internal owner user id (the caller's own — runs are scoped to the authenticated user). Treat as an opaque identifier; do not log/forward outside an authenticated context.

progress.description: Live progress while `status` is `pending`/`running` (#692): the latest phase/page-count event streamed by the run. Null once the run is terminal, or if no progress event has been recorded yet.

AuditRunListItem.description: Audit run as returned by the list endpoint. Also the shared base for the single-run `AuditRun` schema, which composes this plus `userId`/`orgId` via `allOf` — so the common fields live in exactly one place. Nullable fields are unset until the run progresses.

healthScore.description: Rounded score from the persisted `health_score` DB column (an integer). The unrounded float is available as `report.healthScore` on `GET /v1/agent-runs/{id}/report`.

AuditRunReport.description: Summarized report data + top scored issues for a completed run, wrapped under `report`.

healthScore.description: The precise overall score from the report (a float, e.g. 82.5), read straight from the report JSON. Intentionally a `number` here — the rounded `integer` `healthScore` on `AuditRun`/`Report` mirrors the persisted DB column, while this is the unrounded source value.

topIssues.description: Up to 25 failing/warning checks, fails first.

AuditReport.description: The full audit report payload produced by the squirrelscan engine. Only the high-signal top-level fields are documented here; the complete schema is validated by the hosted API. Extra top-level fields are accepted but ignored, while the documented fields below are validated and must conform.

EntityMapSummary.description: Site-wide totals. Describes the WHOLE audit even when the response is filtered.

danglingCount.description: Edges pointing at an `@id` no crawled page declares.

stableIdShare.description: nodesWithStableId as a 0-1 share of nodeCount.

pageLocalCount.description: Entities tagged `pageLocal` — what a graph hides by default.

nodesWithoutIdCount.description: Entities with no `@id` declared on more than one page: the identity finding. An entity seen on a single page is not counted.

conflictCount.description: Entities carrying at least one conflicting property. Counts entities, not properties.

EntityMapNode.description: One entity, collapsed across every page that declares it. Every string here comes from site-declared JSON-LD and is untrusted; escape before rendering.

key.description: Identity the builder settled on: the resolved `@id` when the site supplied one, otherwise a synthetic type+name key.

id.description: The resolved `@id`, or null when the entity declared none.

occurrences.description: How many times the entity was declared across the crawl.

pages.description: Declaring pages, sorted and capped; the remainder is in morePages.

conflicts.description: Properties whose value differs between occurrences.

danglingRefs.description: Outgoing `@id` references from this node that nothing declares.

pageLocal.description: True when the entity describes one page rather than the site's subject matter: Question, Answer, BreadcrumbList, ListItem, WebPage, and an ImageObject with no name. These are hidden unless `include_page_local` is set.

EntityMapEdge.description: A typed reference from one node to another. A dangling target is deliberately absent from `nodes`.

predicate.description: author, publisher, mainEntity, about, isPartOf, sameAs, logo, offers, …

dangling.description: True when no crawled page declares the target.

EntityMapResponse.description: The entity-map document plus the context the endpoint adds under `meta`.

pages.description: Per-page contributions. Empty on hosted maps: the published copy drops it and the summary carries what a reader needs from it.

filtered.description: True when a query filter removed at least one entity.

counts.description: Post-filter totals. Compare against `summary` to see whether this is a subset.

pageFilterIncomplete.description: True when a `page` filter ran against a map containing an entity whose declaring-page list was capped. The result may be missing entities that really are declared on the requested page, because the omitted URLs are not in the document. Always false when no `page` filter was given.

backfilled.description:
Summary counters that were RECONSTRUCTED because this map was published before the field existed, so they are estimates rather than site totals.

`summary` normally describes the whole audited site while `nodes` may be a projection capped at 750 entities. A reconstructed counter can only be computed from the stored entities, so on a large site it reads low next to its un-reconstructed siblings. Render those fields as "at least N", or hide them, rather than as site totals.

Empty on a map published by a current CLI. Entity-level `pageLocal` is reconstructed exactly and is never listed here.

pageCount.description: Total declaring pages, including any beyond the `pages` cap.

outbound.description: Edges from this node, including dangling references.

pricing.description: Credit cost table keyed by feature.

pricingVersion.description: Monotonic version of the pricing table.

members.description: Members of the organization. Only returned to callers who are themselves members (the handler enforces membership and returns 404 otherwise — non-members never see this list).

userEmail.description: PII — a fellow member's email address. Intentionally exposed so org members can see their teammates (the dashboard team view renders it); access is gated by the membership check above. Treat as sensitive: do not log, cache publicly, or surface outside an authenticated org-member context.
